en: bake a batter in hot fat

does: Pours a thin egg batter into fat that is already smoking hot in a very hot oven, so that it sets and puffs at once into a crisp, golden, hollow pudding.
how: Heat a thin layer of fat in a metal tin in a very hot oven until it smokes.
Work fast: pull the tin out, pour in the batter, and it should sizzle at once.
Shut the door and do not open it until the pudding has risen and turned deep golden and crisp.

cues.text: A loud sizzle the moment the batter meets the fat.
Puffed, deep golden edges that stand high above the tin.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring the batter into fat that is only warm, so that it soaks in and stays flat and greasy.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the fat is smoking before the batter goes in.

mistakes.mistake: Opening the oven early, so that the pudding sinks.
mistakes.fix: Keep the door shut until it is well risen and brown.

comes_after.why: The pudding needs a smooth, rested batter.

variant_of.differs: The batter goes into fat that is already smoking hot in a very hot oven and the door stays shut, so it puffs at once instead of baking slowly.
